notes: All three chapters render the same shared satisfaction state, green bar and small report-evidence line. No precise satisfaction percentage is printed. The main score chart, actual metric counts and weight evidence are retained.

Satisfaction is derived from completed reports: Level 1 target met 44; Level 2 reports 60/70/77/82/86; Level 3 publications 90/93/95. Qualitative states progress from Satisfied to Very satisfied to Delighted, with larger early and smaller later increases. These narrative positions do not measure learning.

Chapter baselines match exactly, including standalone previews. Selecting/swapping, dragging/confirming/resetting weights, observing, replaying and comparing never add satisfaction. Near-even and uneven allocations receive the same publication increment. Students retain specific negative behaviour and Learning at risk.

A production combined playthrough verified all report milestones, both chapter handoffs, Level 1/2/3 replays, a more uneven second allocation and the third reference. A separate near-even first allocation earned the identical increment. Fresh visits reset according to the existing entry point.

Normal-motion browser playback verified the bar fills smoothly from its preceding position over one second. Reduced motion is immediate. 320/390/1366px standalone layouts, shared type and no overflow passed; desktop and mobile screenshots were visually reviewed.

Existing suites passed for all 20 priority trios, inclusive 10-point near-even boundaries, linked confirmation, free second attempts, all actual comparison records, manual Observe, name/sound/trio handoffs, real-time audio, hidden-page holds and fresh-visit behaviour. No player Restart, administrator login or Design Lab transition was added.

All four latest previews and the two-version review ZIP were rebuilt together. Release tests verified exact downloaded ZIP hashes and byte equality, then played through the individual and combined production HTMLs. Versioned historical archives and validation reports remain unchanged.

Managed Chromium uses an in-memory HTTPS origin for exact offline production bytes because local file navigation is blocked. Direct file opening in the user browser, classroom load capacity and finished partner videos were not tested. The preview still stops at the final theory placeholder.
